nodes.question: What factors are essential to clarify in order to understand ecological processes governing microbial community assembly?
nodes.answer: It is essential to clarify the spatial and temporal turnover of microbial communities as well as the key factors driving these changes.
nodes.paragraph: This study provides insights into how fertilization shapes microbial communities and indicates that organic fertilization enhances the resistance of microbial communities under changing environmental conditions. Keywords Rhizosphere microbes Bacteria Fungi Growth stages Temporal stability 1 Introduction Understanding the mechanisms shaping the diversity, sta- bility and assembly of microbial communities is critically important, as this knowledge can significantly contribute to the prediction of shifts in their ecosystem functions in response to climate change and agricultural management practices (Ladau and Eloe-Fadrosh 2019). Microbial com- munity that exhibit higher ability to resist environmental disturbance and to recover from disturbance is described as microbiome stability (Allison et al. 2008). To understand the ecological processes governing microbial community stability and assembly, it is essential to clarify the spatial and temporal turnover of microbial communities (Ladau and Eloe-Fadrosh 2019) as well as the key factors driv - ing these changes. nodes.question: Which study references the influence of plant growth stages on soybean microbiomes?
nodes.answer: The influence of plant growth stages on soybean microbiomes is referenced in the study by Moroenyane et al. 2021.
nodes.paragraph: 2018; Malard et al. 2021; Ma et al. 2023), their temporal scale dynamics remain less well understood. Previous studies have reported that plant growth stages significantly influence both soil and plant microbial com- munities. For example, the composition and function of the maize plant microbiome varied with plant growth, with bac- teria and fungi playing different ecological roles at different growth stages (Xiong et al. 2021 ). Similarly, plant growth stages modulate assembly processes in soybean microbiomes (Moroenyane et al. 2021) and drive the temporal and spa- tial dynamics of bacterial communities in the rhizosphere of Vigna subterranea (Ajilogba et al. 2022). In sugar beet, microbial diversity, composition and function in various com- partments shift across different growth stages, with the strong- est effect observed in the rhizosphere (Li et al. 2024). These temporal variations may be due to changes in soil moisture, available nitrogen and phosphorus, and root exudates (Brock - ett et al. 2012; Hirsch and Mauchline 2012; Ng et al. 2014; Li et al.

nodes.question: According to Chen et al. (2019), what has a stronger influence on bacterial communities compared to fungal communities?
nodes.answer: Chen et al. (2019) demonstrated that plant growth stages have a stronger influence on bacterial communities than on fungal communities.
nodes.paragraph: Additionally, bacterial communities were reported to have a higher microbial temporal stability compared to fungal communities (Lange et al. 2023), whereas Chen et al. (2019) demonstrated a stronger influence of plant growth stages on bacterial communities than on fungal communities. Despite these progresses, our knowledge of the relative temporal sta- bility of bacteria and fungi remains unclear, especially under different chemical and organic fertilizer regimes. Sorghum, known for its exceptional tolerance of drought and barren (Gao et al. 2020), is the 5th most widely culti- vated cereal crop worldwide and a vital resource for ensuring food security. The rhizosphere is an important compartment for microbiomes that can predict crop yield and protein (Liu et al. 2023) and is more significantly affected by organic and inorganic fertilization treatments relative to other crop com- partments (Sun et al. 2021). In this study, we characterized sorghum rhizosphere community structure of bacteria and fungi, based on a long-term field experiment initiated in 2011. This study aimed to (i) whether organic fertilizer enhanced temporal variations in rhizosphere bacterial and fungal com- munities; and (ii) assess the stability of both bacterial and fun- gal communities across different sorghum growth stages.
